apps.loved: A lock screen widget with a daily word and etymology provides constant passive exposure to new vocabulary without any effort. Sentence examples help clarify usage.
apps.weak: Without exercises to practice the words, new vocabulary does not stick. Some definitions are inaccurate. One word per day is too slow for meaningful vocabulary growth.
apps.whoFor: Those who enjoy discovering new words passively and want a low-effort daily vocabulary habit as a supplement to other study.

apps.title: Word of the Day・Vocabulary
apps.verdict: A vocabulary app built around a daily word with illustration and contextual examples. The concept worked well until the 2024 update: the art illustrations were removed, streaks were wiped, and saved words disappeared. The linguistic quality of word selection is high, but one word a day is too slow for meaningful vocabulary growth.
apps.loved: Rare and precise words for writing and journalism: the app selects vocabulary that genuinely enriches expression. Pre-update art illustrations are fondly remembered by long-term users.
apps.weak: The 2024 update broke streaks, removed saved words, and replaced original illustrations with generic images. Core features users relied on were changed without notice. One word per day is insufficient for systematic vocabulary building.
apps.whoFor: Writers, journalists, and advanced English users who want daily exposure to precise, high-value vocabulary as a supplement to their reading.

apps.title: ELSA Speak - English Learning
apps.verdict: Was an interesting tool for pronunciation training with phoneme-level analysis. After a major update the interface was completely redesigned, pronunciation features were buried behind an AI avatar, and voice recognition became unreliable. The app is slow and frequently freezes.
apps.loved: Detailed phoneme-level pronunciation breakdown. A large topic library. In the old version there was a clear progression through specific English sounds (TH, SH, AE).
apps.weak: Speech recognition does not catch correct pronunciation and marks it wrong. The AI avatar layer obscures the pronunciation tools that made the app useful. Frequent freezes and slow performance.
apps.whoFor: Pronunciation-focused English learners who were using the old version. The new version is hard to recommend until stability improves.

quotes.text: This app started with promise, but quickly devolved into a frustrating experience that feels like a complete rip-off. The core functionality, voice detection, is shockingly unreliable. Even in a perfectly quiet, closed room, with absolutely no background noise, the app struggles to accurately detect my voice.

apps.title: AlgoApp - Flashcards
apps.verdict: A flashcard tool that deliberately mimics the AnkiMobile name. The repetition algorithm is weaker than the original, the interface has degraded through a series of updates, and sync is unreliable. Works as a wrapper for your own decks but contains nothing language-specific.
apps.loved: Users who figured it out appreciate folder-based deck organization, support for images and audio in cards, and multi-device functionality.
apps.weak: Weaker SRS algorithm than AnkiMobile. Interface has degraded over updates. Sync is unreliable across devices. No language-specific content or built-in vocabulary.
apps.whoFor: Those who want a free Anki-like SRS tool and already have their own decks or know where to find pre-made ones.

apps.title: EWA Kids: English for children
apps.verdict: A children's English course through pictures and simple phrases. Due to a technical bug (a dog appearing at the end of every lesson for a month) progress is not tracked. Audience is preschool-age children and there is no real data on learning outcomes in reviews.
apps.loved: Bright visual design and simple interactive tasks appeal to children. Parents from Spanish-speaking countries note that the child willingly reopens the app.
apps.weak: Does not show whether the child will learn to speak: no pronunciation feedback, no structured progression beyond basic words. The persistent bug blocked progress tracking for an extended period.
apps.whoFor: Parents of preschool-age children who want a visually appealing English exposure tool for young children with no prior English.

apps.title: HelloTalk - Language Learning
apps.verdict: A language exchange platform with native speakers where correction tools and dialect filtering are useful, but finding a partner focused on actual study rather than socializing is rare.
apps.loved: Country and level filters help find the right dialect. Built-in message translation works directly in the chat without switching apps. Voice rooms provide live speaking practice.
apps.weak: Most incoming contacts turn into flirting or spam. Finding a study-focused partner is rare and time-consuming. The app facilitates contact but does not structure learning.
apps.whoFor: Intermediate and above learners who want conversational practice with native speakers and are willing to filter out non-study contacts patiently.

apps.title: Open English: Learn English
apps.verdict: A platform with live native-speaker teachers and grammar progression by level that in theory allows you to reach conversational fluency, but all levels are mixed in the same classes so beginners end up with advanced learners.
apps.loved: Live sessions with native speakers available around the clock, a clear grammar progression by level, and immediate teacher feedback during class.
apps.weak: Promises fluency in a year but most who complete the course do not reach it. Mixed-level classes mean beginners are grouped with advanced learners. Support response times are slow.
apps.whoFor: Motivated learners willing to pay for live instruction who understand that the timeline promises are optimistic.

apps.title: English language: Learn & Play
apps.verdict: A gamified idiom review format will appeal to those who already know the basics and want variety, but it is useless for beginners, audio is synthetic, and the content library runs out within a few sessions.
apps.loved: The gamified card format appeals to those who want to review familiar idioms in a fun way without reading a textbook.
apps.weak: Idioms presented without context. No native-speaker pronunciation. Grammar is completely absent. Content is exhausted within a few sessions with no path forward.
apps.whoFor: Intermediate and above learners who want a light, playful way to review English idioms they already know roughly.

apps.title: Tandem: Practice Languages
apps.verdict: A language exchange platform with native speakers where built-in in-chat translation is convenient, but reaching actual live conversation is increasingly difficult due to a verification process that can take up to 47 days.
apps.loved: Built-in message translation directly in the chat sets Tandem apart from competitors and lets you look up words without leaving the conversation. The user base is diverse in language and geography.
apps.weak: The platform connects people but does not teach language. Most contacts turn out to be spammers or people with non-study intentions. The verification wait is too long.
apps.whoFor: Intermediate and above learners with patience for filtering contacts who want genuine conversational exchange with native speakers.

apps.title: Jumpspeak | Language Learning
apps.verdict: An AI conversation trainer with role-play scenarios. The idea is right: practicing speech through thematic dialogues. The execution is poor: voice models are low quality, role-play sessions break and swap lines between characters, and audio is unclear. The company's billing policy is described as aggressive and dishonest.
apps.loved: A few users noted the right concept: thematic conversations beat memorizing phrases. One of the few tools where you respond to a scenario rather than fill in a blank.
apps.weak: Voice model quality is poor. Role-play sessions crash and characters swap lines. Audio is unclear. Billing described as aggressive by multiple users independently.
apps.whoFor: Would suit intermediate learners wanting AI role-play practice if the technical and billing issues were resolved.

apps.title: LingoTok - AI Language Tutor
apps.verdict: The concept of an AI conversation tutor works, but the execution is unreliable: constant drop-outs, AI accent that does not match the target language, and progress that does not save. Amid widespread complaints about unauthorized billing the substantive problems fade into the background.
apps.loved: The live conversation format with pronunciation correction appeals to the few users who have no technical problems. Several users noted progress in French and Spanish comprehension.
apps.weak: Constant session drop-outs. AI accent does not match the target language. Progress fails to save. Billing complaints are widespread and independent.
apps.whoFor: Those willing to navigate significant technical instability for AI-driven conversational practice in French or Spanish.

apps.title: BetterSpeak: AI Language Tutor
apps.verdict: An AI tutor with the idea of daily conversational practice without a schedule, but the microphone frequently fails to register answers and pronunciation correction is unreliable.
apps.loved: The idea of a daily 15-minute speaking session with an AI at any time appeals to those who managed to reach real content and start a dialogue.
apps.weak: The microphone frequently fails to register responses and the dialogue breaks down. Pronunciation correction is inconsistent and misses errors. Language selection is limited. Progress does not save reliably.
apps.whoFor: Intermediate learners who want flexible daily AI conversation practice and can tolerate significant technical friction.

apps.title: Voice Language Translator Pro
apps.verdict: The app positions itself as a voice translator rather than a language learning tool. Basic translation works, but advertised features (movie subtitle translation) are absent. It builds no language skills whatsoever.
apps.loved: Basic text translation quality is described as acceptable. The interface is simple.
apps.weak: Does not teach language at all: no content, no lessons, no feedback. A translator, not an educational tool. Voice packs for some languages are incorrect.
apps.whoFor: Those who need basic translation and are not looking for language learning.

apps.title: Dictionary.com: English Words
apps.verdict: A dictionary that was the gold standard for years lost its core value after a change of ownership: saved word collections were deleted without warning, definition navigation is broken, and search returns wrong entries.
apps.loved: The thesaurus and related definitions in one place used to let you move from word to word through chains of meaning, which made it an indispensable deep vocabulary tool for years.
apps.weak: Personal word collections that users built over years were deleted without notice. Definition navigation is broken. Search sometimes leads to the wrong entry. Core features that defined the product no longer work.
apps.whoFor: Formerly for serious English vocabulary study and writing. Currently the product's reliability is too low to recommend.

apps.title: LangLearn: AI English Tutor
apps.verdict: An AI chat for spoken English practice that reduces anxiety before live conversation, but the content does not match what is shown in promotional videos, speech recognition is unreliable, and you cannot change the language being studied.
apps.loved: Dialogue with an AI tutor reduces anxiety for beginners before live interaction. Learning through songs and conversational examples worked for those who reached it.
apps.weak: Speech recognition is acknowledged as weak even by users satisfied with the app overall. Advertised features are absent. Cannot switch the study language. Session quality is inconsistent.
apps.whoFor: Anxiety-prone beginners who want a low-pressure AI partner for English speaking practice before attempting live conversations.

apps.title: 10 Minute English
apps.verdict: Advertised content such as audiobooks and film subtitles is absent from the app. No grammar explanations and no speaking practice. The app teaches only vocabulary through flashcards.
apps.loved: A few users who reached the app without technical issues noted a convenient interface for word learning and realistic dialogue examples in certain lessons.
apps.weak: Content does not match what promotional materials promised. Core advertised features are absent. Speaking practice and grammar are entirely missing. Technical issues block many users from reaching even the available content.
apps.whoFor: Those who only need basic vocabulary flashcards and are not misled by the broader feature promises in marketing.

scenarios.name: Adults whose goal is to speak
scenarios.job: Move from understanding to a real conversation: reach the level where you can hold a conversation with a native speaker rather than pass a test
scenarios.gap: They need to try speaking in the situation the language is being learned for, and see where the difficulties are. An exercise on single words and a live conversation test different skills.

scenarios.name: Learners with one specific sticking point
scenarios.job: Close one precise gap: conjugations, kanji, hiragana or the pronunciation of specific sounds, rather than starting the language from scratch
scenarios.gap: After working on conjugation, writing or a sound, a person needs a suitable next step. That is better decided by the job and by an attempt to apply it than by an obligatory subscription renewal.

scenarios.name: Users of rare languages
scenarios.job: Find clear learning material for the language or writing system they need and for their own communication situation.
scenarios.gap: Authors look for material for a specific language and for family or everyday communication. What matters is the right variety of the language and a clear start.

scenarios.name: Socially anxious learners
scenarios.job: Practice speaking without the fear of making a mistake in front of a live person: get out of the state where the knowledge is there but panic blocks the conversation
scenarios.gap: The person needs practice where mistakes cost no embarrassment. It is worth checking whether the chosen scene helps them speak for themselves and then carry that experience into the situation they need.

scenarios.name: People coming back after a break
scenarios.job: Quickly reactivate a language they had a few years ago: not learn from scratch but restore the basics and get to a working level
scenarios.gap: After a break, skills come back unevenly. What matters is starting from a suitable exercise and being able to skip what is known without hiding the gaps in other skills.
